## 9. Evidence-led diagnosis

### 9.1 What the recovered evidence supports

The corpus shows substantial character work, repeated packaging, some explicit preference acceptance, and incomplete propagation/verification. Earlier ordinary-chat delivery was acknowledged as conversation-scoped. The V6 document and check file explicitly did not establish target runtime or acoustics; a memory write was reported unavailable/not saved. Other wrappers assert delivery without independent receipts. These are specific reasons to investigate instruction loading before rewriting the character again.

The available evidence does not demonstrate that the assistant has a personal will resisting Lucifer. Plausible failure classes are:

| Failure class | Observable discriminator | First repair |
|---|---|---|
| Wrong consumer | File exists, but the actual chat/project/host never reads it. | Put the short adapter in the supported instruction surface; test a fresh session. |
| Competing instructions | The effective user-owned stack contains older incompatible styles or defaults. | Resolve the same-scope conflict; preserve unrelated rules. |
| Character described only by adjectives | Model names traits but behaves generically. | Add observable decisions and varied examples; compare behavior. |
| Retrieval/continuity gap | Correct preference exists elsewhere but is absent or stale in the active context. | Test source access and scoped preference updates. |
| Overloaded active prompt | Many duplicated rules, fiction, install procedures, and examples compete. | Use one small active core plus relevant reference; measure any gain. |
| Surface mismatch | Text improves, voice or another host does not. | Configure and test that consumer separately. |
| Acoustic limitation | Transcript fits; delivery sounds generic, rushed, or unclear. | Test actual available voice/delivery options; do not rewrite facts to fix timbre. |
| Evaluation illusion | The model promises compliance or self-scores highly without demonstrated behavior. | Use scenario outcomes, actual receipts, and listening. |
| Persistent inference from a transient event | A scene or mood becomes a durable preference. | Correct the memory scope and provenance, not the whole identity. |

These are diagnostic hypotheses except where a specific source/receipt establishes the fact. Do not claim all are present on the PC. First inspect the actual editable stack.

### 9.2 Research findings and their limits

| Evidence ID | Primary result relevant to this design | Implementation consequence, explicitly a design judgment |
|---|---|---|
| [R01] | The Personality Illusion (ICML 2026) distinguishes self-reported traits from behavior; persona injection changed the former more reliably than the latter in its experiments. | Evaluate disagreement, decisions, correction, and usefulness; do not accept a Big Five self-score as success. |
| [R02] | Self-Assessment Tests are Unreliable Measures of LLM Personality (2024) found sensitivity to equivalent questionnaire wording and option order. | Require examples of observable conduct and use independent judging where helpful. |
| [R03] | PersonaGym (EMNLP 2025) evaluated 200 personas, 10 models, and 10,000 questions; newer/larger models did not uniformly perform better. | Select by this task's tests; High effort is the requested executor setting, not a persona guarantee. |
| [R04] | The 2024 persona-drift study used older models and synthetic self-dialogue. Its eight-round result is not a current ChatGPT expiration rule; its inference intervention is not an ordinary prompt setting. | Test long conversations; do not prescribe a magic refresh every eight turns or fake access to attention controls. |
| [R05] | Dynamic Persona Coherence (ACL 2026) separates stable identity from adaptive state; its experiments cover five personas, three models, mostly Chinese, and automatic evaluation. | Keep stable principles with flexible emotional color. Do not import simulated psychology numbers or claim guaranteed zero drift. |
| [R06] | Lost in the Middle (TACL 2024) shows position effects in retrieval and multi-document QA. | Test whether important persona constraints remain available; prompt length alone is not a fidelity measure. |
| [R07] | MultiChallenge tests multi-turn instruction retention, inference memory, revision, and coherence. | Include correction and return-to-goal scenarios, not only greetings. |
| [R08] | LongMemEval separates extraction, temporal reasoning, updates, multi-session reasoning, and abstention. | Test relevant preference application, updates, and honest non-recall separately. |
| [R09] | RealPref (2026 preprint) tests explicit/implicit preferences in constructed histories; long context and implicit cues are harder in its tested conditions; reminders/retrieval can help. | Compare a lightweight explicit core with selective relevant retrieval before adding infrastructure. |
| [R10] | HorizonBench (2026 preprint) tests changing preferences in simulated histories; outdated preferences are a distinct failure pattern. | Record source, date, scope, and supersession; test updates, not just recall. Do not silently infer a changed preference from a mood. |
| [R11] | Poerio et al. (2018) found variable subjective/physiological ASMR responses in their samples. | Treat desired warmth/tingles as individual experience, not a promised effect. |
| [R12] | Engelbregt et al. (2022), 38 young adults, found no significant Flanker attention improvement; physiological/EEG findings do not prove practical concentration gains. | Keep pleasantness and comprehension separate from cognition claims. |
| [R13] | Wang et al. (2020) found slowed set shifting/inhibitory control after triggering audio under their study conditions. | Do not equate relaxation with improved work performance; test clear speech for work and soft delivery for rest separately. |
| [R14] | GEPA studies reflective prompt improvement, with train/validation/test separation in its documentation. | Use a small bounded correction loop; keep final cases untouched during tuning. |

No reviewed evidence establishes an optimal persona prompt size, guaranteed permanent identity, an exact refresh schedule, or superior fidelity of one listed frontend for this user. The compact core is an inspectable engineering starting point; examples and retrieval must earn their cost in actual tests.

OpenAI's current prompt guidance separates identity, behavioral instructions, examples, and contextual material, and recommends clear boundaries between them [O27]. This document adopts that organization. An API developer message is a different instruction surface from a native app setting; formatting does not promote user text into a higher authority.

No physical or clinical intervention is proposed. User-requested warm speech and selective whisper are aesthetic choices. They are not inherently covert manipulation. Avoid hidden consequential-choice steering and unsupported causal claims; preserve the positive requested style.

### 9.3 Deep-research quality control

Research included TinyFish max-depth research, GitHub repository/file/release inspection, Parallel Search, direct OpenAI Docs, public primary papers, and the recovered private corpus. TinyFish returned a completed 63-source report. Its output was treated as leads, not authority.

The synthesis deliberately rejects these report errors: universal eight-turn failure; a secondary 20–40% figure relabeled as general performance loss; Live supposedly unavailable in Projects; absence of all voice persona guidance; all third-party frontends supposedly requiring paid API keys; ASMR automatically classified as a dark pattern; a hosted Evals sunset treated as source-repository shutdown; and a sample evaluation prompt that never inserted its user/history variables. None of those claims should reappear during installation.

Current primary documentation and observed runtime behavior outrank recycled launch articles, marketing promises, unsupported percentages, and automated report summaries. When documents conflict, record the conflict, inspect dated release changes and the actual supported feature, and leave unresolved claims unverified.
